Alex — thanks for the clear numbers and the spreadsheet, that’s super helpful. Recap below and a couple of quick answers so you can loop procurement.

Quick answers up front:
- At ~250M tokens/month, Hosted API can be in the ballpark of $40–$60 / 1M tokens depending on model choice and any committed volume discounts.
- Batching, choosing a slightly smaller model for non-critical routes, and prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts are our top levers to reduce unit cost.
- Hosted peak TPS: we offer burst capacity across our regions but there are soft limits on sustained TPS per account. For your numbers (8 TPS sustained, ~12 TPS bursts) that’s within typical Hosted capacity; we’ll confirm with ops. If you anticipate consistent sustained higher TPS we usually recommend a Dedicated reservation.

Notes / unit economics back-of-envelope (high level):
- Example pricing bands (Hosted):
  - Redwood-large (higher quality): ~$80 / 1M tokens
  - Redwood-medium: ~$45–$55 / 1M tokens
  - Redwood-small (low-cost): ~$25–$35 / 1M tokens
- Assuming a mix where 60% of tokens hit medium and 40% hit small, blended ~ $42 / 1M tokens -> ~ $10.5k/month at 250M tokens.

Alex — quick technical follow-up and suggestions I added to the spreadsheet (see Drive link above). Main items: 

1) Caching: Recommend prefix caching for any repeated system prompts and common user prompts — can reduce token counts by ~15–30% on chat-heavy flows.
2) Batching: For your batch processing windows (ETL-like jobs), we can increase throughput by using micro-batching in the client; this lowers per-token CPU overhead and can reduce effective $/1M by ~10–20% for that workload.
3) Model selection: use Redwood-medium for conversational quality; route lower-critical background tasks (summaries, metadata generation) to Redwood-small.
4) Rate limits: Hosted accounts have soft per-account sustained TPS limits (operationally enforced); short bursts are supported up to ~3x the sustained. For anything above sustained thresholds we recommend a Dedicated reservation.

I also flagged a couple of rows in the token spreadsheet where prompt engineering can trim token usage (shorter system messages, stop sequences).

If you want, I can schedule a 30-min tech sync with our infra team to prototype a small batch job and show expected latency and cost delta.

—Marissa
